chunks: We gave Moses the Book, and made it a guidance for the children of Israel that they should not take another protector apart from Me.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Book given to Moses in relation to divine guardianship?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the continuity of divine guidance, positioning the Torah as a precursor to the Quran while establishing the foundational principle of Tawhid (monotheism) through the command to take no Wakil other than Allah. It reflects the broader Islamic narrative where previous scriptures are acknowledged as valid guides for their respective communities, yet the ultimate reliance remains solely on the Divine. This reinforces the concept of divine sovereignty, where God is both the source of law and the ultimate protector.
